name: Cetus Dwarf
tagline: An isolated Local Group spheroidal — beyond both giant halos, it evolved nearly untouched.

facts.label: Isolation
facts.value: Outside the MW and M31 halos

history: The Cetus dwarf is one of the Local Group's few spheroidals that is not a satellite of either big spiral — it lies outside the Milky Way and Andromeda halos and has presumably been quiescent for most of its history. That isolation makes it precious: its uniformly old, metal-poor stellar population records how dwarf galaxies evolve when left to themselves, a control case against which the tidally processed satellites are compared.
